verdicts.reason: Nearly identical left-to-right layouts (phone → Glow. → SHOP SOLSTICE). Both have the same flaws: the logo is shrunk to a tiny, orphaned dot jammed against the phone's bottom corner, the CTA is small and pushed to the right edge, and the decorative circle is clipped at the top. B's phone nearly touches the top and bottom edges, while A keeps slightly more margin around the phone.

In A, the tiny logo is stranded on its own in the gap between the phone and the headline, near the bottom edge. A's phone almost touches the top and bottom of the canvas, and the CTA hugs the right edge, so the composition feels lopsided. B has the same cramped phone and small CTA, but its logo at least sits next to the phone as a group.

A just shrinks the portrait original into the middle of the banner. The CTA and logo become unreadable specks, the headline is tiny, the decorative circle floats in the middle of the canvas, and about 70% of the width is dead space. B is properly rearranged into a horizontal banner. Its remaining flaws are minor: a tiny orphaned logo, a phone cramped against the top and bottom edges, and an undersized CTA at the far right.

A flips the reading order so the CTA comes first, before the headline and product. Its logo floats on its own below the CTA, and the phone is jammed against the right, top and bottom edges while also overlapping the decorative circle. B keeps a logical order (product → headline → CTA), but it still has the tiny orphaned logo, a phone cramped against the edges, and a small CTA hugging the right edge.
